chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Muḥammad ibn Aslam, from Hārūn ibn al-Jahm, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

“Whichever wet nurse of a people kills an infant belonging to them while she is asleep, and she turns over onto him and kills him, then the blood-money is upon her, from her own property alone, if she had only undertaken wet-nursing in pursuit of honor and pride. But if she had only undertaken wet-nursing because of poverty, then the blood-money is upon her ʿāqilah.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood-money owed as legal compensation for a wrongful death
key_terms.ظِئْرِ: a wet nurse who suckles and cares for another family’s infant
key_terms.عَاقِلَتِهَا: her paternal kin group legally responsible for paying the diyah in such a case

ai.seo_question: Who pays the diyah if a wet nurse accidentally kills a child while sleeping?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a wet nurse who accidentally kills an infant by rolling onto him while asleep. It distinguishes between whether she took up wet-nursing for status and pride or out of poverty, affecting whether the diyah is paid from her own property or by her ʿāqilah.
